newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish PM says aims for budget surplus by 1998.
newsitem.headline: Swedish PM says aims for budget surplus by 1998.

text.p: The Swedish government aims to have a budget surplus from 1998 and halve unemployment to four percent by 2000, Prime Minister Goran Persson said on Tuesday at the opening of parliament.
"To halve unemployment is the government's foremost priority, overshadowing all other tasks," Persson said.
Swedish finance minister Erik Asbrink had said earlier in a newspaper article that he aimed to have a permanent budget surplus from 1998.
The Swedish government is to release its budget on Friday.
He said price and wage increases should not prevent the government's aim to halve unemployment.
"The labour market has an extraordinarily big role in this," Persson said.
Persson said public sector finances should not only be in balance but should be in a surplus at the time of the next general election in September 1998.
"Savings across the board are increasing our ability to act with more flexibility and give the public welfare system a needed stability," he said.
He said the government's priorities in relation to health care and education remained unchanged and ahead of other state benefits.
"As unemployment falls and state finances strengthen, this will provide more room for moves to improve income distribution without jeopardising the budget's consolidation," he said.
Persson also told parliament that the phasing out of nuclear power should begin before the next general election and continue at a steady rate.
"It will happen in such a way that it will not jeopardise the competition between power intensive industries," Persson said.
In other moves, Persson said the government would set up a grant programme as part of a billion crown investment to strengthen cooperation within the Baltic region.
The new programme, called the Visby programme, aimed to widen academic programmes for students and researchers in the three Baltic states, Russia, Poland and Sweden.
He also announced government plans to set up a special authority to combat abuse of the social welfare and tax system.
